intro: A good claim is one clear, arguable point that a debater can actually defend.

criteria.name: One idea
criteria.test: Makes a single arguable point. Giving a reason for that point is fine; adding a second, separate complaint is not.
criteria.bad: Phones cause cheating, distraction, and texting in class.
criteria.good: Phones let students cheat on tests.

criteria.name: Takes a side
criteria.test: Clearly argues for or against the motion, rather than describing the topic neutrally.
criteria.bad: Lots of students bring phones to school these days.
criteria.good: Schools should ban phones because they make cheating easy.

criteria.name: Concrete
criteria.test: Names a specific situation, person, or mechanism instead of staying abstract.
criteria.good: Students look up answers on their phones in the middle of a test.

criteria.name: Contestable
criteria.test: A reasonable person could disagree. Not a truism, and not just the motion repeated with no reason attached.
criteria.good: Phones cause enough cheating that banning them is worth the hassle.

exemplar: Schools should ban phones during exams because students use them to look up answers mid-test.
